test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: If the selling price of a bed is 3-times of initial, then the profit is 4-times of initial. Find the initial profit percentage (in %).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Initial Selling Price (SP₁)** be x and **Cost Price (CP)** be y.

Initial Profit (P₁) = x − y.

New Selling Price (SP₂) = 3x, New Profit (P₂) = 3x − y.

Given: P₂ = 4 × P₁ ⇒ 3x − y = 4(x − y) ⇒ 3x − y = 4x − 4y ⇒ x = 3y.

Initial Profit % = [(x − y) ÷ y] × 100 = [(3y − y) ÷ y] × 100 = 200%.

**∴ The correct answer is 200%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **SPₙₑw = 3 × SPₒₗd** and **Profitₙₑw = 4 × Profitₒₗd**.
Formulas: Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/699095b90db7c9426973acffa7cce9a47d0adbbc757133acaa392a4928d5d947.png] 
⇒ Let **Initial Profit** be P and **Initial Cost Price** be CP.
⇒ SP₁ = CP + P.
⇒ SP₂ = 3 × SP₁ = 3(CP + P) = 3CP + 3P.
⇒ New Profit = SP₂ − CP = (3CP + 3P) − CP = 2CP + 3P.
⇒ According to question: 2CP + 3P = 4P ⇒ 2CP = P.
⇒ Profit% = (P ÷ CP) × 100 = (2CP ÷ CP) × 100 = 200%.

**∴ The correct answer is 200%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Selling Price Relationship

When the **Selling Price** changes, the change in **Profit** is exactly equal to the change in Selling Price, because the **Cost Price** remains constant.

Profit Percentage Formula

Profit% is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise: Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.</p
